components.name: Primary Button

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Every control is labelled; the Field component generates the id so the association cannot be skipped.
components.html: <label class="ds-field-label" for="ds-plate">Truck plate</label><input class="ds-field" id="ds-plate" value="AB1234CD" />
components.css: .ds-field-label { display: block; color: #cbd5e1; font: 500 0.875rem/1.4 Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; margin-bottom: 0.375rem; } .ds-field { width: 100%; background: rgba(51,65,85,0.5); color: #fff; font: 700 1.125rem/1.4 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.05em; padding: 0.625rem 0.75rem; border: 1px solid #475569; border-radius: 0.5rem; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: #94a3b8; } .ds-field:focus { outline: none; border-color: transparent; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #3b82f6; }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Visit status. The hue is declared once in status-machine.ts; nothing re-derives it.

components.name: Visit Card
components.description: A truck in the queue. The plate leads, everything else supports.
components.css: .ds-card { background: rgba(30,41,59,0.5); border: 1px solid rgba(51,65,85,0.5); border-radius: 0.75rem; padding: 1.25rem; transition: border-color 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: #475569; } .ds-card-plate { color: #fff; font: 700 1.125rem/1.2 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.05em; } .ds-card-meta { color: #94a3b8; font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; margin-top: 0.25rem; }

components.name: Side Navigation Item
components.description: Side rail from md up; the same items become a fixed bottom bar below it.
components.html: Queue
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 0.625rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; color: #cbd5e1; font: 500 0.875rem/1 Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background 0.15s ease-out, color 0.15s ease-out; } .ds-nav-item:hover { background: rgba(51,65,85,0.5); color: #fff; } .ds-nav-active { background: rgba(59,130,246,0.2); color: #60a5fa; }

components.name: Driver Board Row
components.description: One truck on the public panel: plate in large mono, status stripe on the leading edge, dock number on the right. Read at distance, not at arm's length.
components.css: .ds-board { background: #000; padding: 0.5rem; } .ds-board-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; background: rgba(20,83,45,0.4); border-left: 4px solid #22c55e; border-radius: 0.25rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.5rem; } .ds-board-plate { color: #4ade80; font: 700 1.5rem/1.2 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.05em; } .ds-board-dock { background: #16a34a; color: #000; font: 700 1.25rem/1 Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 0 0.75rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; }

components.name: Call Flash
components.description: The one authored moment: the board is taken over for five seconds when a truck is called.
components.css: .ds-flash { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 0.25rem; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #16a34a, #22c55e 50%, #15803d); padding: 1.5rem; } .ds-flash-plate { color: #fff; font: 900 3rem/1 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.05em; } .ds-flash-label { color: #dcfce7; font: 700 0.875rem/1 Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.1em; } .ds-flash-dock { background: #fff; color: #000; font: 900 2.25rem/1 Geist, system-ui, sans-serif; padding: 0.25rem 2rem; border-radius: 0.5rem; animation: ds-pulse 0.5s steps(1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-pulse { 0%, 49% { opacity: 1; } 50%, 100% { opacity: 0.3; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-flash-dock { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Tablo is read in two places that could not be less alike, and the system exists to serve both without pretending they are the same. Inside, a dispatcher works a dark console at arm's length, scanning a board of trucks and docks under warehouse lighting, often on a phone with gloves on. Outside, a driver sitting in a cab across the yard looks up at a small illuminated panel and needs exactly one fact: whether it is their turn, and which dock. The console is dense, quiet and information-first. The panel is loud, sparse and readable at thirty metres. Same palette, opposite volume.

Depth comes from tonal layering, not shadow: one near-black ground with translucent surfaces stacked on it. Colour is functional almost everywhere — a hue on this system means a status, not a mood — which is what lets the single green flash on the driver board carry so much weight. Nothing else in the product is allowed to shout.

The plate number is the product's proper noun. It is always monospace, always the largest thing in its container, and it is the one place where type is doing work rather than decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first by use scene, not by fashion: a warehouse at night and a backlit yard panel
Depth by translucency over one ground; shadows only for things that float
Monospace for identifiers, sans for everything a human wrote
One authored motion moment, and it belongs to the driver

rules.name: The Status Hue Rule
rules.body: A status colour is declared once, in src/lib/status-machine.ts, as a chip pair (accent-300 on accent-500/15). No component re-derives it and no screen invents a hue for a state. Adding a status means adding a row there, not styling a badge.

rules.name: The One Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Proceed Green at full strength appears in exactly one place: the call flash on the driver board. If a second element on any screen is competing with it for attention, the second element is wrong.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Text is never set below Text Secondary on any surface in this product. Slate-500 measures 3.07:1 on a card and fails AA; it is permitted only for non-text decoration.

rules.name: The Monospace Is For Machines Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks an identifier a machine issued: plates, order references, DNs, hashes. It is never used to make prose look technical.

rules.name: The Plate Leads Rule
rules.body: Wherever a visit appears, its plate is the first and largest thing in the container. Carrier, dock and time are support.

rules.name: The Gloved Thumb Rule
rules.body: Anything tapped on a phone gets a 44px minimum box. Controls that only exist on the admin desktop screens may drop to 24px, and nothing goes below that.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: To make something look higher, raise its opacity or its border, not its shadow.

dos: Do take status colour from src/lib/status-machine.ts, and add new statuses there.
Do pair every focus:outline-none with focus:ring-2 — the whole product does this today.
Do set identifiers in Geist Mono and human prose in Geist.
Do give every control a 44px tap box on any screen a phone reaches.
Do keep the driver board to one idea per glance: who is next, and where they go.
donts: Don't set text in slate-500 or darker; it fails AA on every surface here (3.07:1 on a card).
Don't add a drop shadow to convey hierarchy — raise the tonal layer instead.
Don't use a unicode glyph or emoji as an icon; lucide-react is the icon system.
Don't flash anything faster than 3 Hz, and give every animation a prefers-reduced-motion alternative that keeps the information and drops the movement.
Don't let a second element compete with the call flash for attention.
Don't make the driver board responsive; it is a fixed 576x224 panel on a wall.
